title: composite-degradation-sentinel-and-fail-mapper-ci-hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a composite degradation sentinel that aggregates multi-signal regressions into a single CI decision and emits granular failure categories to improve triage speed.
description: Motivation: Flaky PR failures and noisy signal from single-metric gates make triage slow. This change adds a Composite Degradation Sentinel (CDS) that scores a prompt-set across multiple metric families (quality, hallucination, latency, token-usage) and maps aggregated severity into granular failure categories used by CI and the PR reporter. Goals: 1) reduce unnecessary CI noise by requiring correlated degradation across signals, 2) provide per-prompt failure tags (e.g. hallucination-high, latency-regression, quality-drop-medium) so on-call and engineers can route fixes faster, and 3) keep the default config conservative (disabled by default for existing repos) while enabling in our smoke and nightly pipelines for eval-harness. What this PR implements: - New sentinel implementation at eval_harness/sentinels/composite_degradation.py that computes z-score-normalized deltas across metric families, applies configurable weight vectors and a correlation threshold to produce a composite severity score. - A fail-mapper (ci/hooks/fail_mappers/composite_fail_mapper.py) that converts composite scores and per-metric breakouts into a stable set of failure_tags consumed by the CI reporter and the PR status decorator. - An opt-in yaml config parser (eval_harness/configs/sentinels.yaml) and CLI flags for toggling CDS and providing per-repo overrides. - A new lightweight end-to-end smoke test that runs a synthetic prompt-set against a mock baseline and verifies emitted failure_tags and telemetry. - Metrics and traces emitted to telemetry via existing reporter interface (metrics: cds.composite_score, cds.cohort_correlation, cds.per_metric_zscore_*). - Docs and examples: docs/sentinels/composite_degradation.md with configuration examples and recommended weight presets for text-generation vs. reranking workloads. Backwards compatibility and rollout: CDS is behind a sentinel gating flag; the PR transitions nightly-evals to enable CDS in paranoid mode (low false positive tolerance). We also include a migration note for teams that rely on single-metric CI gates, with suggested weight matrices. Related work: builds on prior per-prompt anchor and ensemble gates but focuses on cross-signal correlation to reduce single-metric churn. Links: Linear ENG-9412 feature spec: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9412/composite-degradation-sentinel
commits_summary: 1) initial composite sentinel and fail-mapper implementation; 2) add config parsing and tests; 3) emit telemetry and docs; 4) fix zscore edge-case when sigma=0; 5) CI test fixes after lint failure
review_conversation: Rafael Jimenez: Overall this looks promising. Two immediate asks: (1) can we make the default weight vector explicit in code and docs so teams don't get surprised, (2) add a fallback when all per-metric stddevs are zero to avoid division-by-zero.

Maya Chen: Thanks Rafael. Default weights are now baked in constants with inline docs and also surfaced in sentinels.yaml. I added a numeric-stabilizer in composite_degradation.py (epsilon floor) and a unit test in test_composite_degradation.py.
Sofia Patel: The fail tags look useful, but the names are long. Can we normalize to short machine-friendly tags and keep a human-readable mapping in the PR report?
Maya Chen: Good call. Updated composite_fail_mapper.py to emit compact tags (e.g. hall_high -> 'HALL_HIGH') and included a mapping file used by the PR reporter to expand descriptions in the web UI.
Eliot Zhang: CI lint failed on import ordering and a flake8 warning about unused variable in telemetry_adapter. I pushed a small style fix and removed an unused import.
Maya Chen: Fixed lint issues and re-triggered CI. All CI checks green on the second run.
Rafael Jimenez: Approving after verifying tests and a quick run of nightly pipeline with CDS enabled in paranoid mode.
